sentences.text: Denmark's government has just 82 of 179 seats. And that's normal. Why?
Who can vote? Danish citizens from 18 living in the Kingdom, but not Danes settled abroad.
On the ballot, you put one cross: next to a party, or next to one of its candidates.
Parties above 2% share the seats by votes nationwide.
These 179 MPs form the Folketing, the only chamber. It makes the laws and checks the government.
In 2026, twelve parties got in. The Social Democrats came first, with 38 seats.
The parties went to the King three times to pick a negotiator. After a record 69 days, Mette Frederiksen formed a government.
It runs the country without a majority behind it, as long as no majority votes against it.
And the King? Frederik the Tenth inherited the throne. He signs every law, but can't block one.
Should a government rule without a majority behind it?
